extracted.intended_audience: literate public interested in religion, deism, and religious criticism (late-18th-century philosophical readers)
extracted.subtask_description: A polemical/philosophical essay arguing standards for evaluating religious claims (mystery, miracles, prophecy, scripture) and proposing natural creation and benevolence as the proper basis of religion and morality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of mystery in religion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Religion... cannot have connection with mystery. The God in whom we believe is a God of moral truth, and not a God of mystery or obscurity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religion, considered as a duty, must be on a level to the understanding and comprehension of all; 'mystery' is a fog that obscures truth and is used to bar questions and inquiry. Anything religious that relies on 'mystery' to prevent examination is suspect and an anti-pattern for true religion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracles are unreliable evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Of all the modes of evidence that ever were invented to obtain belief to any system... that of miracle... is the most inconsistent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept miracle reports as proof of doctrine. Seek natural explanations first (examples given: balloons for ascension, electricity/magnetism for sparks and motion, resuscitation for apparent restoration to life, sleight of hand, optical deceptions). Miracles shift burden to the reporter's credibility; it is usually more probable a reporter lies than that nature has been suspended. Reliance on miracles implies weakness or lameness in the underlying doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophecy should be suspected and must be specific to be credible
rubrics_metrics.description: "Prophecy took charge of the future... The third [prophecy] ought always to be suspected."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A genuine prophecy, if it exists, should be expressed in terms that could be understood and not so loose or obscure as to fit almost any subsequent event. Vague, retrofittable, or obscure predictions are not reliable evidence; the ambiguity of prophetic language makes it easy to manufacture post hoc interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed scripture cannot be assumed to be the unaltered word of God
rubrics_metrics.description: "That the idea or belief of a word of God existing in print, or in writing, or in speech, is inconsistent..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate claims of a written/divinely given text against practical transmission problems: lack of a universal language, mutability of language, translation errors, the possibility of suppression, alteration, or fabrication. These vulnerabilities mean printed texts cannot be taken as unimpeachable divine evidence without additional, independent corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: The natural creation is the proper and primary 'word of God'
rubrics_metrics.description: "That the Creation we behold is the real and ever existing word of God, in which we cannot be deceived. It proclaimeth his power, it demonstrates his wisdom, it manifests his goodness and beneficence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observable nature as primary evidence of deity: attributes like power, wisdom, and goodness are manifest in creation and serve as trustworthy grounds for religious belief. Preference is given to evidence that is public, observable, and accessible to human reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral duty measured by imitation of divine beneficence
rubrics_metrics.description: "The moral duty of man consists in imitating the moral goodness and beneficence of God manifested in the creation towards all his creatures."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate moral and religious practices by whether they promote universal benevolence and happiness. Actions such as persecution, revenge, or cruelty to animals violate moral duty. Serving God is construed as contributing to the happiness of the living creation rather than engaging in sectarian austerities or exclusionary practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth rejects crutches; doctrines needing miracles/extra aids are suspect
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is necessary to the full and upright character of truth that it rejects the crutch; and it is consistent with the character of fable to seek the aid that truth rejects."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer doctrines that stand on moral reason and observable evidence without recourse to extraordinary supports (miracles, obscure prophecy, enforced mystery). If a system requires such supports to be believed, treat it as likely fabulous rather than true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictive/calculable phenomena as strong evidence of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: "I have one plain answer to give, which is, that man knows how to calculate an eclipse, and also how to calculate to a minute of time when the planet Venus... will come in a strait line between our earth and the Sun... As therefore, man could not be able to do these things if he did not understand the solar system... the fact of calculating an eclipse... is a proof in point that the knowledge exists."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the ability to make accurate, testable predictions (e.g., eclipses, transits) as strong evidence of true knowledge. Use predictive/calculable phenomena to distinguish reliable scientific or cosmological understanding from mere assertion or fabrication.
